```{r message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(p8105.datasets)

source("source/nsduh_process.R")
source("source/mean_and_sd.R")

set.seed(1236)
```


## Lists!

Prove that lists can have anything

```{r}
l = list(
  vec_numeric = 5:17,
  mat = matrix(1:8, nrow = 2, ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE),
  vec_logical = c(TRUE),
  summary_table = summary(rnorm(1000))
)

l
l[[1]]
l[["vec_logical"]]
l$summary_table
```

## `for` loops

```{r}
list_norm = list(
  a = rnorm(20, 3, 4),
  b = rnorm(20, -14, 20),
  c = rnorm(20, 1000, 10),
  d = rnorm(20, 0, 1)
)
```

Can I get mean and SD for each sample

```{r}
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[1]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[2]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[3]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[4]])
```

Annoying to have them all separate -- do this better so it's quicker/more efficient

```{r}
output = vector("list", length = 4)

for (i in 1:4) {
  
  output[[i]] = mean_and_sd(list_norm[[i]])
  
}
```

## `map` instead

This is better!

```{r}
output = map(list_norm, mean_and_sd)

output = map(list_norm, median)
```

What about map variants

```{r}
output = map_dbl(list_norm, median)
output = map_df(list_norm, mean_and_sd)
```
